comparisons.scheme1_value: Direct cash support to supplement financial needs of landholding farmers for farm inputs and domestic expenses.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Micro loans to help non-farm small business owners (and some farm-related businesses like poultry/dairy) start or grow their enterprises.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Direct cash grant (Rs. 6,000/year) — money given to you, no repayment needed.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Loan (Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 20 lakh) — money lent to you, must be repaid with interest.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers who own cultivable land in their own name (with major exclusions: government employees, income-tax payers, professionals like doctors/lawyers, retired pensioners earning Rs. 10,000+/month).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Self-employed individuals, shop owners, vendors, artisans, small business owners, partnerships, companies — with no major caste/profession exclusions (but must have good credit record).

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 6,000/year paid in 3 installments of Rs. 2,000 every 4 months.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Varies: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (Rs. 50,000–5 lakh), Tarun (Rs. 5–10 lakh), Tarun Plus (up to Rs. 20 lakh) — amount decided based on business need.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Aadhaar Card, land ownership papers, bank account details (Aadhaar-seeded).
comparisons.scheme2_value: For small loans (Shishu): identity proof, residence proof, 2 photographs, business proof. For larger loans: additionally requires bank statements, tax returns, projected balance sheets, and project report.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online via pmkisan.gov.in — enter Aadhaar number, verify with OTP, fill form, upload documents.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Online via udyamimitra.in (linked from mudra.org.in) — register, fill business details, select loan category, attach documents. Can also apply directly at bank branches or via Jan Samarth portal.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) — money goes straight to your bank account every 4 months.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Processed by banks/lending institutions; interest rates vary by lender per RBI guidelines; upfront fees waived for Shishu loans by most banks.

comparisons.scheme1_value: If ANY family member paid income tax in last year, entire family becomes ineligible — even if they own farmland.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Must have satisfactory credit history — defaulters to any bank/financial institution are NOT eligible.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Land must be in YOUR name — renting/cultivating someone else's land does NOT qualify.
comparisons.scheme2_value: NO unofficial agents or middlemen — anyone claiming to be a 'MUDRA agent' is a fraud; apply only through official channels.
Apply: udyamimitra.in | Info: mudra.org.in | Also: jansamarth.in

recommendation: **Choose PM-KISAN if:** You own farmland and need periodic cash support for farming (but watch the income-tax and employment exclusions). **Choose MUDRA if:** You want to start or expand a small business (shop, vendor stall, poultry farm, repair service, etc.) and can repay a loan. MUDRA is a loan, so it requires a business plan and repayment capacity — PM-KISAN is free money but only for farmers. **Disclaimer:** This is AI-assisted guidance based on official scheme documents. Not an official notification. Verify final eligibility with government portals (pmkisan.gov.in / mudra.org.in) or your nearest bank/CSC before applying.
confidence_level: High — all information sourced from official government scheme context.
